summary: Today's digest contains 493 vulnerabilities across 5 sources. 96 zero-day exploits detected, 46 actively exploited from CISA KEV, and 17 Pakistan CERT/NCCS advisories.

OsGeo GeoServer contains an XML injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause the server to read local text files accessible to the GeoServer process or fetch attacker-specified HTTP or HTTPS URLs via a crafted ID parameter in the WFS 2.0 GetFeatureById stored query. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-2026-129245, and CVE-2026-129242 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on an affected GeoServer instance.

GeoServer contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass service-level role checks and invoke operations protected solely by those checks via a request with a prefixed service parameter. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129245, and CVE-2026-129242 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on an affected GeoServer instance.

Drupal Core contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to take over a site via the exposed Drupal installer when the site is in one of the affected unusual or incomplete installation states.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router contain an OS command injection vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID.

Vates Xen Orchestra contains an improper validation of specified type of input vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and perform actions with administrative privileges via a specially crafted authentication token containing an empty JSON object.

Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper authentication vulnerability that could allow an attacker to generate a web report exposing sensitive information, including internal IP addresses, usernames, and store names.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains a path traversal vulnerability that could allow an attacker to access and read underlying server system files via the XML interface.
Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series contains an improper input validation vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to run arbitrary commands on the affected system.

Mitel MiCollab contains a not failing securely vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication controls and perform unauthorized actions.

Mitel MiCollab contains an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component due to insufficient file type validation that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to upload arbitrary files.

Mitel MiCollab contains a weak authentication vulnerability in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to access sensitive information using a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an XML injection vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands using pre-staged malicious content.

Mitel MiCollab contains an improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command (OS command injection) vulnerability in its Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary system commands.

Optimizely Web Experimentation contains an external control of critical state data vulnerability in its account signup flow that could allow an attacker to impersonate existing customer users and modify Project JavaScript. Successful exploitation can result in attacker-controlled JavaScript being distributed through Optimizely-hosted assets and executed in browsers visiting affected customer websites.

Idunno AntiCsrf contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via object injection. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer. Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site.

Project MONAI MONAI Label contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files outside the intended datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution.

N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the LDAP synchronization connection check that allows an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.

Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.

Broadcom VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system.

SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.
BerriAI LiteLLM contains an unprotected alternate channel vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.

Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.

Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.

UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability that allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.

Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.
Microsoft Office Outlook contains a missing user interaction for potentially unsafe action vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience.

Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Load Balancer, Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver (BMA), WAF Control Center (WCC), Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG) contain an OS command injection vulnerability. This vulnerability could allow an authenticated administrator to inject OS commands that execute with root privileges when the crafted timezone value is subsequently processed. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-116606

Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.

Google Chromium contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XML component that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a specially crafted webpage. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.

GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml.
OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux contains an unexpected status code or return value vulnerability that could allow for authentication bypass.
SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability that permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution.
IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations.

SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS 10.5 contain an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability to bypass pointer authentication.

WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.

Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition contain a integer overflow or wraparound vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.

Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software contains an unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

Path traversal in TPM device management in Canonical LXD from 4.8 before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a remote authenticated user with project access to recursively delete arbitrary files and directories on the host as root via a crafted device name during instance or device removal.

In LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2, an improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to write and delete files at arbitrary host filesystem paths as root.

 When a custom storage volume is pushed to a LXD daemon, the snapshot names supplied by the migration peer are never validated and are used to build the filesystem path of each received snapshot. This allows an attacker to place attacker-controlled files into any host directory as root, gaining root-level code execution on the host, and to recursively delete an attacker-chosen path.

In LXD before 5.21.0 and 6.10.0, an OS command injection vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to execute arbitrary code as root on the host.

 The raw.dnsmasq bridge network configuration key is not restricted to server administrators and is copied verbatim into the dnsmasq configuration file, so a user whose project keeps the default features.networks=false can have a bridge network created in the default project with an injected dhcp-script directive. This allows an attacker to make the host dnsmasq execute attacker-chosen code as root on a DHCP lease event and fully compromise the host.

Symbolic link following in imported VM backup config drive preparation in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project-scoped permissions to disclose sensitive host files, including LXD server and cluster keys, and overwrite host files as root via importing and starting a VM backup with a symlinked config directory.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in VM disk migration, export, and attach NBD servers in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an unprivileged local user in the host network namespace to read and modify a guest VM's disk and execute code inside the guest via connecting to abstract Unix sockets while an operation is active.

Improper privilege management during container rebuild in Canonical LXD before 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a local user with container permissions to gain root privileges on the host via rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container so it starts without a user namespace or privileged-container hardening.

Path traversal in proxy and CDI GPU device name handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, and 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with access to a restricted project permitting proxy or GPU devices to read, overwrite, or delete arbitrary host files as root and terminate host processes via crafted device names containing path traversal sequences.

Improper link resolution in image metadata tarball unpacking in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, and 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with a restricted client certificate to write arbitrary host files as root and execute code on the host via a crafted rootfs symlink in an image metadata tarball.

Exposure of sensitive information in token operation events in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user restricted to a project to gain full server access and cancel pending token operations via capturing certificate or cluster join token secrets broadcast to default project event listeners.

Exposure of sensitive information and missing requestor validation in instance, volume, and snapshot migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read migrating configuration and filesystem data and disrupt the migration via capturing per-connection websocket secrets from operation metadata and racing the migration's data channels.

Configuration injection in virtual machine disk device handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with VM creation permissions in a restricted project to bypass low-level VM restrictions and control the root QEMU process via quotes and line breaks in a disk device's guest path.

Exposure of sensitive information in live and stateful migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read a migrating instance's checkpointed runtime state and disrupt the migration via capturing the state connection secret from operation events or queries.

Improper output encoding in Prometheus metrics exposition in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a user controlling a virtual machine to forge host metric labels and break metrics scraping via unescaped guest-controlled filesystem mountpoints and network interface names.

Improper certificate validation in websocket connections in Canonical pylxd before 2.4.3 allows a network attacker to read command stdin and spoof command output via impersonating a remote LXD endpoint.

The Android application "Tokyo Fire Department Official App" contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows a malicious application installed on a user's device to obtain sensitive information from the affected application.

Incorrect authorization in custom storage volume, backup, and storage bucket endpoints in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with a project-restricted certificate or per-object authorization to read, rename, move, replace, or delete other projects' storage resources and bypass cluster group restrictions via missing project or object ownership checks.

Path traversal in container device path resolution and VM disk format detection in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project access, including an unprivileged local user through lxd-user, to read and modify arbitrary host files or Ceph RBD images and gain root privileges on the host via crafted device paths or QCOW2 backing file references.

Insufficient verification of data authenticity in shared image handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user restricted to a single project to export private images, replace public image contents, remove other projects' images, and pin daemon memory via abusing fingerprint-based image sharing, partial fingerprints, and non-expiring push upload tokens.

Untrusted search path and context handling in host-side instance helpers in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access or root inside an unprivileged container to execute arbitrary code as root on the host, read daemon memory, remount read-only shifted disks as read-write, and disrupt other projects' mounts via file API, SFTP, syscall interception, and disk hot-plug operations.

Incorrect authorization in project restriction enforcement in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to bypass project limits and access forbidden storage pools, volumes, network addresses, and CPU resources via instance moves, backup imports with overrides, received snapshots, or unvalidated volatile keys.

Exposure of sensitive information in API responses, exports, and host-side artifacts in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated lower-privileged user or a local host user to read credentials, private keys, and other projects' metadata and inject arguments into Ceph administration commands via unfiltered endpoints, exported configurations, log files, process command lines, and unvalidated bucket parameters.

Incorrect authorization in NIC, managed network, network zone, and ACL handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user of a restricted project or root inside an instance to manipulate host interfaces and firewall rules, read fragments of root-owned files through error messages, and disrupt or intercept other projects' networks and DNS records via unvalidated device and network configurations.

Improper control of code generation and project restriction enforcement in container configuration handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the host, crash the daemon, and alter shared bridge DHCP assignments via image-supplied LXC configuration, concurrent rename races during updates, and unvalidated syscall or hardware address settings.

Incorrect authorization in instance, snapshot, and image operations in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project or per-object permissions to read and modify other clients' resources and execute arbitrary code as root on the host via missing entitlement checks on secondary objects and push-mode container migrations.

Incorrect permission assignment for critical resources in rsync transfer sockets, instance storage directories, proxy socket paths, and disk staging mounts in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an unprivileged local user to gain root privileges on the host, read or modify transferred volumes, alter host file permissions, and inject AppArmor rules via connecting to unauthenticated abstract Unix sockets, running setuid binaries, or racing path and mount operations.

Path traversal in backup, image, storage volume, and migration handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and write arbitrary host files as root and exhaust daemon memory via crafted symlinks, unvalidated path components, or oversized metadata.

Incorrect authorization in TLS certificate trust store and revocation handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated client with a restricted or revoked TLS certificate to gain unrestricted administrative access to the server or cluster via trust-lookup races, forwarded cluster identity headers, CA-issued certificate detaching, or stale revocation and session state.

Improper authentication in OIDC bearer token verification in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a remote attacker holding a token signed by the configured identity provider to authenticate to the LXD API and gain unauthorized control or impersonate users via presenting tokens issued for other applications, ID tokens, or unverified email claims.

Incorrect authorization in backup export and network zone read endpoints in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with view-only access to export instance and custom storage volume backups and read network zone TSIG peer keys via endpoints enforcing only view permissions.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in image template handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and overwrite host block and character devices via importing device nodes in an image's templates directory and accessing them through instance template endpoints.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in optimized ZFS backup imports in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to mount an attacker-controlled filesystem over arbitrary host paths and execute code as root on the host via importing a filesystem ZFS stream declared as a block volume.

Configuration injection in liblxc instance configuration generation in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2, 5.21.10, 5.0.12, 4.0.16 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access or a local user of the LXD user socket to execute arbitrary commands as root on the host via line breaks in instance configuration keys and values.

Authentication bypass by spoofing in bridged NIC MAC filtering in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a privileged user inside an instance sharing a managed bridge to intercept and deny inbound network traffic addressed to a neighbour instance via sending frames with a spoofed source MAC address before filtering drops them.

Improper link resolution before file access in recursive file pull in Canonical LXD before 4.0.15, 5.0.11, 5.21.9, and 6.8 on case-insensitive client filesystems allows an authenticated user with write access to an instance directory or custom volume to write arbitrary files outside the target directory and execute code as the operator via case-variant symlinks.

Improper authentication in the guest API connection handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a root user inside an unisolated instance to impersonate another instance and read its configuration, metadata, and devices across project boundaries via holding open connections across PID wrap-around.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in the instance file transfer API in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and write arbitrary host block or character devices, compromise the host, and hang file transfer requests via importing device nodes or named pipes outside /dev in an image or backup and opening them on a stopped instance.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in image and backup metadata handling in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2, 5.21.10, 5.0.12, 4.0.16 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and overwrite arbitrary host files, access other projects' data, and block the daemon via importing device nodes, hard links, symlinks, or named pipes.

A vulnerability was detected in ONNX ONNXMLTools up to 1.16.0. This affects the function get_set_node of the file onnxmltools/utils/visualize.py of the component Model Visualization. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A flaw has been found in ONNX ONNXMLTools up to 1.16.0. This impacts the function visualize_model of the file onnxmltools/utils/visualize.py. This manipulation of the argument producer_name causes basic cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A vulnerability has been found in code-projects Simple Laundry System 1.0. This affects an unknown function of the file viewdetailforuser.php. The manipulation of the argument serviceId leads to sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy_files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy_files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

The Forminator Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Approval Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.3 via the forminator_replace_custom_form_data() function. This is due to the function expanding the {all_fields} merge tag before {account_approval_link}, so a submitter-supplied field value containing the literal string {account_approval_link} is resolved into the real activation URL, including the secret activation key, in the user confirmation email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain the activation link for their own pending registration and activate the account via the ?page=account_activation&key= endpoint, bypassing the manual approval configured on the registration form. Exploitation requires a user-registration form with manual approval enabled and a user confirmation email that includes the {all_fields} merge tag (the default template). Note: On WordPress Multisite installations with site registration enabled, the self-activated account also becomes the Administrator of the subsite created during registration.

The Translate WordPress with Weglot 2.0 – Multilingual AI Translation plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target site to permit anonymous comment posting (comment_registration disabled) and have at least one Weglot destination language active; on sites with comment moderation enabled, an administrator must approve the carrier and trigger comments before the injected script executes for subsequent visitors.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via deserialization of untrusted input that is injected into the Memcached object cache through request Host header key truncation. The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The Simple Calendar – Google Calendar, Events, & ICS Feeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_ics_feed_file (DESCRIPTION property inside the uploaded .ics)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the victim to click the attacker-controlled link rendered in the event description, as the javascript: href payload does not fire on page load alone.

The Easy Google Maps by Supsystic – Custom Markers, Clustering & Map Themes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file (tmp_name / name / type)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The plugin globally widens the site's upload MIME allowlist to permit SVG files via an upload_mimes filter, meaning the attack surface exists for all uploads site-wide regardless of theme or other plugins.

The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'extraclasses (also icon, iconcolor, number)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The existing sanitization is ineffective for this context: wp_kses_post preserves bare double quotes (no HTML tags are required in the payload), and wp_json_encode correctly escapes the value for the JavaScript string-literal layer but the reconstituted double quote remains live when Leaflet.ExtraMarkers builds its inner HTML, allowing a single-quoted shortcode attribute value to close the HTML attribute and inject attacker-controlled event handlers.

The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'overview-latlng' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by Author-level users because WordPress does not apply kses filtering to post custom fields on save, allowing raw HTML payloads such as event-handler attributes to be stored verbatim and later reflected through the unescaped debug output path.

The Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'start_date' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires the victim — who must hold the manage_woocommerce capability (administrator or shop manager) — to both open the attacker-crafted URL and click the start_date input field on the Export Tools page, as the injected payload is delivered via an onclick handler rather than a page-load event. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload must be encoded as C-style escape sequences (e.g. \x3c/\x3e) at storage time so that wp_kses_post — applied on save for users lacking unfiltered_html — passes it through without stripping angle brackets; WordPress core's shortcode_parse_atts() then decodes the escapes into real HTML characters at render time.

The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'embedcode' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The plugin grants the Subscriber role the edit_aiovg_videos and edit_published_aiovg_videos capabilities on activation, and save_meta_data() accepts the 'embedcode' type without checking current_user_can('unfiltered_html'), meaning any Subscriber can store a malicious shortcode containing a data: URI in the hls attribute that hls.js later processes and Plyr writes into the DOM via innerHTML.

The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'price_disabled_msg' setting in versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 The uni_cpo_save_settings_data() AJAX handler applies html_entity_decode() to the output of uni_cpo_sanitize_text(), which itself already runs html_entity_decode() before wp_kses(); this double decode allows a double-entity-encoded tag to pass wp_kses as inert text and then be re-materialised as live HTML before being stored in the _cpo_price_disabled_msg post meta and later echoed via do_shortcode() on the single-product page without further escaping. The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the `SwpmLevelForm::role()` function applying only `sanitize_text_field()` to the user-supplied `role` parameter with no allowlist, permitting the `administrator` role to be stored verbatim into `swpm_membership_tbl` and subsequently applied to a member's WordPress account via `$user->add_role()` inside `update_wp_user_role()` — also without any role allowlist — when the `swpm_membership_level_changed` action fires. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to elevate their own WordPress account to the full Administrator role, gaining complete site control including plugin installation, user creation, and all other administrator capabilities. Exploitation requires that an administrator has first lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default of `manage_options` to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts` (Contributor), `edit_published_posts` (Author), or `edit_pages` (Editor), which is a non-default granted-access configuration; the bulk screen's nonce protection (`swpm_bulk_change_level_nonce_action`) does not mitigate the issue because the nonce is emitted on the same page the delegated lower-role user can already reach. The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files.

In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, the decompress_xpi_thread() function extracts XPI archives (ZIP format) to disk using libarchive. For each archive entry, the output path is built by concatenating the intended extraction directory with the raw pathname from the archive:

    full_path = g_build_filename(path, archive_entry_pathname(entry), NULL);
    archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, full_path);
    ret = archive_write_header(ext, entry);

The libarchive extraction options did not include ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT or ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS. As a result, archive entries containing parent-directory traversal sequences (for example "../../../../../.bashrc") are written outside the intended web_extensions extraction directory.

A malicious .xpi file can therefore overwrite arbitrary files writable by the user running Epiphany, such as ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. This can lead to persistent code execution on subsequent shell startup or GNOME login.

Exploitation requires the victim to install or open a crafted .xpi file. The reporter notes that opening an XPI can trigger extraction even when the WebExtensions feature is not enabled by default.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.rc.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2143, which adds ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT and ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS to archive_write_disk_set_options().
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2922

A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form.

In embed/web-process-extension/resources/js/ephy_autofill.js, getSelector() builds a CSS selector by directly interpolating an element's id attribute:

    path.unshift(`#${el.id}`);

When the user selects an autofill entry, the browser process in embed/ephy-web-view.c previously constructed JavaScript using sprintf with the selector embedded in single quotes:

    EphyAutofill.fill(PAGE_ID, 'SELECTOR', FILL_CHOICE);

Because SELECTOR comes from attacker-controlled page content and is not escaped, a crafted id such as a'); PAYLOAD; var _=(' breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript when the script is evaluated.

The injected code runs in Epiphany's private autofill script world, which hosts EphyAutofill credential APIs and password manager save/request handlers. The reporter demonstrated a proof of concept that injects credentials into another domain and uses Ephy.permissionsManager to enumerate domains with special permissions. Full exfiltration of all saved passwords was not demonstrated but may be possible given the privileges of this context.

Exploitation requires the victim to visit a malicious page, right-click on a form field, and choose an Autofill context menu item. This is a deliberate user action but does not require installing software or entering credentials manually.

Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.beta.
Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2147, which replaces sprintf-based script evaluation with a WebKit user message and jsc_value_object_invoke_method() passing the selector as a typed string argument.
Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2921

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-portal. When a sandboxed application invokes Spawn() and maps two different file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() can fail. Affected Flatpak versions do not handle that failure, so a file descriptor that was open inside flatpak-portal (commonly the unfiltered D-Bus session bus) can be passed into the subsandbox. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app with no special privileges can use this to escape the sandbox.

The backend language switch action (quick_change_language) of the JTL-Shop administration backend is executed without a CSRF token check, and the supplied language value is neither validated against the installed backend languages nor encoded on output. The value is stored in the session and in the account data of the administrator and rendered without output encoding in JavaScript strings and HTML attributes of backend pages. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in administrator who opens a crafted web page; the code can perform actions with the privileges of that administrator.

The OPC (OnPage Composer) start menu, which JTL-Shop shows to logged-in backend users on storefront pages, writes the current page identifier (which contains the search term on search pages) and further values into single-quoted JavaScript strings without escaping. A single quote in the search term terminates the string. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a backend user who opens a crafted link while logged in to the backend in the same browser; the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend session token contained in the same script to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers do not receive the start menu and are not affected.

The access rules of JTL-Shop (export/.htaccess and export/backup/.htaccess) release files with the extensions gz and zip for the export directory without withdrawing this release in the subdirectory export/backup, in which the shop stores database dumps and file backups. As a result, backup files in this directory can be downloaded without authentication by anyone who knows or guesses the file name. Up to version 5.5.5 the names of database backups consist only of a timestamp; from version 5.6.0 they contain a random component, which does not replace access control. The backups contain the complete shop database (customer data, orders, password hashes) and, for file backups, files of the shop. The access rules are only evaluated by Apache. On installations where another web server, for example nginx, delivers static files such as gz and zip directly (including nginx in front of Apache), the files remain accessible even with the corrected rules, unless the directory is blocked at server level.

The country manager page of the JTL-Shop administration backend (/admin/countries) writes the request parameter activeSortOrder without output encoding into a single-quoted JavaScript string and into HTML attributes. The overview page requires no CSRF token. An unauthenticated remote attacker can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a logged-in backend user who opens a crafted link in the same browser (the session cookie carries no SameSite attribute by default); the code runs with the privileges of that user and can use the backend token of the same page to send requests to the backend. Visitors and customers are not affected.

In Eclipse Krazo Extensions up to and including 3.0.0, AsciiDocViewEngine passes MVC model values to Asciidoctor as document attributes without encoding them. Asciidoctor substitutes attribute references after it escapes HTML special characters and before it processes inline macros. As a result, attacker-controlled model values end up in the output as raw HTML and can inject AsciiDoc inline macros. This allows cross-site scripting in applications that render untrusted data through AsciiDoc views.

MONEO ERP exposes the Ping method of its _slave JSON-RPC service over WebSocket as @rpc.openpublic, so it can be called without a valid session. The method's only guard compares the calling application name with "_login", but that value is taken from the client-controlled params.appname field of the request. When the check passes, Ping stores an attacker-chosen session ID, user number and company in the server session store, and subsequent session validation accepts that session. An unauthenticated remote attacker can therefore create a valid session as any user, including administrators, in any company (tenant) hosted on the server and invoke authenticated RPC methods with that user's privileges, gaining read and write access to that company's data.

Lookyloo is a web-based malware analysis and sandboxing platform. The pull-from-remote-instance feature allows a user to request a previously captured sample from another Lookyloo instance by specifying the target instance's URL and a capture UUID. Prior to the fix, the only restriction on the target URL was a check that the hostname, if it was a literal IP address, was not in a private range. Hostnames that resolved to private or internal addresses were not blocked, and no authentication or allowlist was enforced for anonymous users. This allowed any unauthenticated user to direct the Lookyloo server to issue HTTP requests (HEAD to the root path and GET to /json/<uuid>/status, followed by a capture download) to arbitrary internal or external hosts, effectively enabling a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack. An attacker could use this to probe internal network topology, access captures stored on internal Lookyloo instances, or leverage the server as a proxy to reach otherwise unreachable services. The vulnerability is in the website/web/__init__.py module, specifically the __get_remote_capture function and the associated pull endpoint. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of capture data and internal service information from Lookyloo instances that are not intended to be publicly accessible.

Flowintel contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its HedgeDoc case-notes integration. When a user with editor or administrator privileges associates a HedgeDoc URL with a case, the application later issues a server-side HTTP GET request to that URL to retrieve note content. Before the fix, the stored URL was used directly without validation of its scheme, host, port, path, or userinfo, and the HTTP client followed redirects by default with no connect or read timeouts.

An authenticated attacker could therefore cause the Flowintel server to issue requests to arbitrary internal or external endpoints (for example, cloud instance-metadata services, internal management interfaces, or other intranet hosts) and receive the response body, or follow a redirect chain to an unintended destination. The absence of timeouts also permitted resource-exhaustion against the server's outbound connection pool.

Preconditions:
- An authenticated account with editor or administrator role on the target case.
- The HedgeDoc integration feature is enabled (no explicit configuration gate existed before the fix).

Impact:
- Disclosure of sensitive data served by internal or cloud-metadata endpoints.
- Potential denial of service through unbounded outbound requests.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

A **Type Confusion** has been found in the dns_to_dnsp_convert() function in dnsdata.c of the DNS server RPC module in the **Samba** package. The function copies an HINFO record from the management request into the stored DNS record without converting the request name into the two strings the stored record uses. A low-privileged network attacker or user in the DnsAdmins group adds an HINFO record through the DNS management interface. The directory process that handles the add also serves the directory's other remote calls. That process exits, which disconnects the clients that were using it, and the directory service starts a replacement process. Another add of the same kind crashes the process that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that process is replaced, so repeating the add keeps the directory remote-call service from staying available.

When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and configured to trust incoming X-Forwarded-For headers, in addition to the use of the proxy protocol being enabled between DNSdist and one of its backends, an outgoing TCP connection could be wrongly reused for a query received over the same incoming DNS over HTTPS connection but with a different X-Forwarded-For header, causing the backend to consider the query as coming from the same remote client than the first query received on the outgoing connection.

When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and configured to trust incoming X-Forwarded-For headers, and the reverse proxy placed in front of DNSdist does not replace existing X-Forwarded-For headers but merely append a new header to the query, the first header was used by DNSdist instead of the last one, making it possible for a client to spoof its own IP address.

When DNS over HTTPS is enabled and a caching HTTP reverse proxy is used in front of DNSdist, it is possible to pollute the cache of the HTTP reverse proxy by sending DNS over HTTPS GET queries with a body. DNSdist should either refuse the query or ignore the HTTP body, but instead was processing the content of the HTTP body rather than the query present in the HTTP path.

An attacker can trigger a large memory use by cancelling QUIC streams while DNSdist is retrieving the response from its backend. Instead of releasing the memory corresponding to the cancelled stream right away, DNSdist was mistakenly keeping it around until the end of the QUIC connection.

An attacker can trigger a synchronization issue on outgoing TCP connections between DNSdist and its backend by sending oversized DNS over HTTPS queries. This could cause the backend to refuse queries, send a server failure, or just close the TCP connection.

An attacker might be able to forge its own source IP, smuggle DNS records or bypass EDNS options filtering via a specially crafted DNS query when EDNS Client Subnet is enabled between DNSdist and its backend.

The MCUmgr SMP client matched an incoming response to a pending command in smp_client_response_discover() (subsys/mgmt/mcumgr/smp_client/src/client.c) using only the 8-bit sequence number and the operation. It did not check the transport the response arrived on, or the group and command ID. smp_process_request_packet() hands every MGMT_OP_READ_RSP/MGMT_OP_WRITE_RSP packet received on any SMP transport to smp_client_single_response(), so a response from any SMP peer could complete any pending client command.

On a device that is both an SMP server (for example over Bluetooth LE or UDP) and an SMP client (CONFIG_SMP_CLIENT, for example using img_mgmt_client to update a companion MCU over UART), a peer on the server transport can send up to 256 forged response packets while a client operation is pending and have one of them accepted as the reply from the managed device. Non-matching responses are dropped silently. The response path bypasses the server command handlers, so restricting which server groups a peer may use does not prevent it.

The attacker can forge the results of client operations. For example, a forged image-upload offset makes img_mgmt_client_upload() report success after only part of the image was sent, a forged image-state response can report arbitrary versions or flags, and any pending command can be forced to fail. No memory corruption results: the response callbacks bound-check the decoded data. The target's own image validation limits the result to failed or suppressed updates and disrupted management operations. The fix restricts matching to commands sent on the same transport with the same group and command ID. Responses from a different peer on the same transport are still not distinguished.

dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() in subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c looks up the pending query to cancel by DNS id plus a hash of the name the caller originally asked for. When a reply contains only a CNAME, the resolver sends a new query for the alias and overwrites the slot's query_hash with the hash of the alias name. After one or more CNAME hops, cancelling by the original name silently fails with -ENOENT and the query stays pending.

zsock_getaddrinfo() (exec_query() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c) passes a pointer to its stack-local ai_state as the resolver callback context. When its semaphore wait times out, it calls dns_cancel_addr_info_with_name(), ignores the result, and returns. The CNAME re-query restarts the resolver timer, so a CNAME-only response that arrives more than about 100 ms after the query lets the getaddrinfo() wait expire first. The cancel then fails and getaddrinfo() returns. An attacker who can supply DNS responses can trigger this reliably: a malicious or compromised DNS server, an on-path attacker, or any host on the link for mDNS/LLMNR lookups. The device only has to resolve a name with getaddrinfo().

When the orphaned query later times out, dns_resolve_cb() writes the status and calls k_sem_give() on the dead stack frame. If the attacker answers the alias query instead, the callback copies attacker-supplied address data through a stale ai_arr pointer read from the reused stack. The result is a kernel fault (denial of service) or memory corruption in the calling thread's stack and whatever memory the stale pointer references.

The system call verifier z_vrfy_k_thread_stack_space_get() in kernel/thread.c checked the result of K_SYSCALL_OBJ(thread, K_OBJ_THREAD) with the CHECKIF() macro instead of K_OOPS(). CHECKIF() compiles to if (0) when CONFIG_NO_RUNTIME_CHECKS is selected, and becomes an assertion when CONFIG_ASSERT_ON_ERRORS is selected. In both cases, the kernel-object validation result for the user-supplied thread pointer is ignored, or is a no-op when assertions are disabled.

On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE, CONFIG_INIT_STACKS and CONFIG_THREAD_STACK_INFO plus one of those check modes, a user-mode thread can call k_thread_stack_space_get() with an arbitrary pointer. That pointer can be a fake struct k_thread in its own memory, or a thread object it has no permission on. z_impl_k_thread_stack_space_get() then dereferences thread->stack_info in supervisor mode and scans memory starting at the attacker-chosen stack_info.start.

The syscall returns the number of leading 0xAA bytes at that address. This gives an unprivileged thread a limited oracle on arbitrary kernel or peripheral memory, and allows privileged reads of attacker-selected addresses, including MMIO. No write primitive results. The default CONFIG_RUNTIME_ERROR_CHECKS configuration is not affected. The fix replaces the CHECKIF() with K_OOPS() so the object check is always enforced.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the OAuth token exchange for custom datasources, which sends requests to an unvalidated, user-configured access_token_url. Authenticated users can trigger the authorize_oauth2 endpoint to reach loopback, cloud metadata, or private network services, with internal response bodies reflected in some API error responses.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery protection bypass because getSSRFProtectionOptions passes its safe resolver as dnsLookup instead of lookup. Attackers controlling datasource hostnames can use DNS rebinding in REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth requests to reach blocked private addresses.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ssrf-protection.ts that fails to classify NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48) and 6to4 (2002::/16) IPv6 addresses embedding internal IPv4. Authenticated users can set REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth data-source URLs to attacker hostnames whose AAAA records resolve to these forms, bypassing pre-request and dial-time guards to reach cloud metadata and internal hosts.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the n8n, nocodb, baserow, couchdb, elasticsearch, influxdb, and databricks datasource plugins, which skip the validateUrlForSSRF check. Authenticated builders, or unauthenticated visitors of public apps with templated URLs, can supply internal URLs or hosts to read cloud metadata credentials and internal service responses.

Heym before 0.0.154 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the workflow execute endpoint: anonymous workflows run as any signed-in caller, without an access check, using that caller's credentials and global variables. Authenticated attackers can lure signed-in users to a GET execute link for an attacker-owned anonymous workflow, which the SameSite=Lax session cookie authenticates. The attacker then reads the victim's decrypted credentials from the workflow's run history.

Heym from 0.0.95 before 0.0.154 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to run script on the application origin by publishing HTML output mapper workflows. Attackers can set a workflow to anonymous GET and share the /api/workflows/{id}/execute link, causing visitors' browsers to send authenticated API requests to read or modify their workflows, credentials, and settings.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::handle_write in libnetutil/massdns.cc that dereferences freed request objects after writes complete. Attackers controlling or on-path to a DNS server can send timed DNS responses with forged ICMP port-unreachable messages to crash scans, disclose memory, or hijack execution.

Nmap before 7.992 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in DNS::ResolverImpl::process_request in libnetutil/massdns.cc that frees still-referenced requests when rescheduling after DNS server disconnects. Attackers answering for at least two configured DNS servers can force a disconnect and send a precisely timed response to crash the scan, possibly enabling code execution.

Nmap before 7.992 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Nmap Scripting Engine because nse_main.lua does not explicitly seed Lua's math.random generator. Malicious scanned hosts can observe math.random-derived values in NSE script traffic during -sC scans, brute-force the seed, and recover a heap address that weakens ASLR.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of privileges.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Authentication Bypass by Spoofing vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Remote execution.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information exposure.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Filesystem access for attacker.

A security flaw has been discovered in eosphoros-ai DB-GPT up to 0.8.3. This affects the function editor_sql_run of the file packages/dbgpt-app/src/dbgpt_app/openapi/api_v1/editor/api_editor_v1.py of the component Editor SQL Run API. Performing a manipulation of the argument db_name results in authorization bypass. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

libexpat through 2.11.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in defineAttribute() of lib/xmlparse.c that fails to detect duplicate non-ID #IMPLIED or #REQUIRED attribute declarations. Attackers can supply a crafted XML document with repeated ATTLIST declarations in an internal DTD subset to cause quadratic CPU consumption in storeAtts() during parsing.

django-allauth 65.17.0 before 65.23.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in truncate_ip() that collapses all IPv4-mapped IPv6 clients into one shared rate-limit key. Unauthenticated attackers on dual-stack deployments can exhaust per-IP limits for login, signup or password reset, blocking legitimate IPv4 users.

Leo through 6.8.10 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by embedding pickled data in unknown XML attributes of .leo outlines. Attackers can place a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a <t> or <v> element attribute that resolveUa passes to pickle.loads, executing code with user privileges when the outline is opened.

FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain host tokens from status/hostgetkey.php by supplying a host MAC address. Attackers can present the token to service/hostinfo.php to retrieve decrypted Active Directory join credentials and Windows product keys during deployment windows.

Zettlr before 4.11.0 fails to validate URI schemes in Markdown link targets, allowing attackers to launch arbitrary registered protocol handlers via Electron shell.openExternal without confirmation. Attackers can craft documents whose Ctrl/Cmd-clicked links use smb:// to leak NTLM credential hashes on Windows or invoke custom protocol handlers with attacker-controlled parameters.

HCIPy through 0.7.1 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .pkl files to read_field, read_grid or read_mode_basis. Because hcipy/util/io.py selects pickle by file extension and calls pickle.load, a __reduce__ gadget in a pupil, apodizer, PSF or mode-basis file runs code with the user's privileges.

Detoxify 0.5.3 through 0.5.4 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_checkpoint that allows attackers to execute code by supplying a crafted checkpoint file. Attackers can embed a pickle __reduce__ gadget in a .ckpt file loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False to run code with the user's privileges.

JSONSchema2PoPo2 through 3.0.3 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject Python code by supplying JSON Schema default or format values that are written unescaped. Attackers can place a single quote in a string property default to break out of the literal in the generated __init__ signature, executing injected code when the generated module is imported.

Dreamweaver Desktop is affected by a Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code. Exploitation depends on conditions beyond the attacker's control and requires user interaction in that a victim must open a malicious file. Scope is changed.

smalot/pdfparser before 2.14.0 contains an inefficient algorithmic complexity vulnerability that allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by submitting a crafted PDF with deeply nested unbalanced parentheses in a content-stream string. Attackers can exploit the regex-based string isolation loop in PDFObject::formatContent(), which rescans growing content on each pass to produce O(n^2) processing time, causing a small PDF to stall or exhaust PHP worker resources for seconds to minutes.
